subject.title: fix: show readable session names across Windows UX

question: Should cron, heartbeat, subagent, ACP, hook, harness, dreaming, and other background sessions be hidden by default across the tray, dashboard selection, and chat picker, with only the Sessions page providing an opt-in background view?
rationale: Readable titles address the reported UX problem, but changing which existing sessions remain visible and selectable is a broader navigation policy that tests cannot determine and that the linked issue already marks as needing product judgment.

options.title: Approve filtering after proof
options.body: Keep the proposed default hiding and Sessions-page toggle, but require native current-head proof and confirmation of the finalized upstream presentation contract before merge.

options.title: Limit scope to titles
options.body: Preserve current session visibility everywhere and defer background-session filtering to a separately reviewed product change.

options.title: Pause for Gateway contract
options.body: Hold the Windows PR until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106832 lands, then refresh parsing, compatibility tests, and native proof against the final schema.

recommendation.title: Approve filtering after proof
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed default hiding and Sessions-page toggle, but require native current-head proof and confirmation of the finalized upstream presentation contract before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest available history across the Windows Gateway client, tray UX, localization, and release-validation surfaces affected by this decision.
